item: A ratchet classifies every loop in src/database whose back-edge sits outside the cleanup around it; two of them were reachable from a main thread and are converted; two comments stop attaching a timing to a phase
refs: PR #1501; audit 0.5.0 A-012 part 2 and A-027; follows PR #1489 and R234, R237
summary: A-012 part 2: tests/test_database_loop_heads_are_classified.py lists the ten scopes in src/database whose loop back-edge lies outside an enclosing with, try/finally or except BaseException/KeyboardInterrupt, each with who runs it (worker-only or event-loop), and fails on a new such head without a row and on a stale row. Rows are keyed by qualified name; module and class bodies count; only the body of a with or try counts (a finally also covers a handler and an else); a handler named through a variable or constant reads as catching; a code object no scope has a name for fails closed; an anti-vacuity test pins each shape. The review of the first draft found two rows wrong: corpus_lease.active_leases is reached on a main thread by src/monitoring/release_run_fresh_restore.py (run_restore -> wait_for_quiescence, a subprocess in the server's process group), and pool_watch._live_rows by whatever thread times out on a pool checkout; both loops are converted to the guard-clause form and removed from the table (behaviour unchanged, harm today near nil: that child exits). The worker-only classification of the ten that remain rests on callers found by grep, not on thread starts traced line by line (inferred, labelled so in the test); a row covers its whole function, so a new loop added to a listed function passes unseen, and tests/test_worker_only_callers_pinned.py is the stronger check for the two functions it pins. A-027: two fts.py comments said 981 s then 1,645 s on a 130 GB corpus for the FTS rebuild; SCALE_ROADMAP P0.4 records the unlock as a whole (two consecutive boots on 2026-07-09; the 11.7 GB / 268,241-article database is the first export's) with no split by phase, and says the 130 GB is the data folder of which about 120 GB is unidentified, so the comments no longer attach either figure to the rebuild; they cite the live validation of the fix instead (602 ms in RELEASE_0.2_GATE.md; 323 ms on 1,048,725 articles / 21.0 GB on 2026-08-12). Comment-only apart from the two loop conversions. NOT touched: docs/ledger/OPEN_QUEUE.md:619 still quotes the old wording and gate item 32 in RELEASE_0.5_GATE.md still says the wording stays; Plan owns the gate file and the queue is protected prose, so both are for their owners.
